subject: [PATCH v2 2/5] memcg: force charges from reclaim before trying the limits

2026-10-31.patch_summary: This patch modifies the memcg (memory cgroup) charging mechanism to force charges from reclaim before trying the limits. This change is necessary because reclaim can charge memory, and if it fails at a limit, it can lead to issues such as increased sleep time for tasks in direct reclaim and kswapd recording overage that it never handles. The patch checks for PF_MEMALLOC before trying the limits, allowing reclaim charges to skip memory.high enforcement and preventing kernel threads from queuing high_work. This change also has effects on how charges are counted and handled by cgroups.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Michal Hocko noted that the patch introduces a potential race condition by checking PF_MEMALLOC before forcing charges, and suggested moving this check after the charge is forced to avoid false events.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that their original patch was not sufficient to address the issue, tested an alternative approach (trying charge after reclaim) but found it had its own problems and is still working on a solution.

Author acknowledged a fix is needed for the issue of raised_max_event being removed, which would cause forced charges to raise MEMCG_MAX again.

Author acknowledged that the patch causes an event to be raised when a charge exactly matches the limit, and this is different from current behavior.

Author acknowledged that the patch needs a change to prevent multiple ancestors of a cgroup from receiving events when reclaim charges exceed limits, and stated they want to keep their current version.
sentiment_signals: stated desire to keep current version
reviews.raw_body:
I actually tested your version as well i.e. after the charge. It is just
as racy and it has some additional issues which are inlined.

---

First, raised_max_event can't go. Since 374f65b14819 rejected charges use it
too, and without it forced charges that already raised MEMCG_MAX before reclaim
raise it again.

---

Second, !mem_cgroup_margin() is true at usage == max, so a charge that fits
exactly raises an event (unlike today).

---

Third, we definitely need a break here otherwise every ancestor at its limit gets
an event which does not happen today.

I want to keep my current version.
